extracted.intended_audience: fiction writers, critics, and students of the craft of the novel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on choosing and applying narrative method (dramatic scene vs. narrator/omniscience) to render characters, inner life, scope, and effects in novels. Emphasizes when to dramatize, when to narrate, and how to let scenes embody meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dramatization (enactment of remote manifestations)
rubrics_metrics.description: By no picture of them but by an enactment of their remotest manifestations — that is how their strength, their bulk, their range in a harassed existence is represented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer showing inner forces by staging their outward effects in scenes rather than by direct description. Example: Milly’s buried troubles are given 'solidity, weight, a third dimension' when the author skirts round them and lets their remotest manifestations appear in action and circumstance. Anti-pattern: merely underlining or stating the inward trouble directly, which cannot produce the same effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Express thought through looks, gestures, and scene
rubrics_metrics.description: The story that is concerned with the impact of experience upon a mind can be enhanced to the pitch of drama, because thought has its tell-tale gestures and its speaking looks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use actors' visible and audible signs — gestures, fleeting expressions, broken phrases, setting and movement — to 'enact' thought and feeling. Let the dialogue and the physical particulars reveal the suppressed appeal or inner state instead of explicit exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify the presence of a narrator (economy of narration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the presence of a seer and a recorder is made a value in itself, contributing definitely to the effect of the subject, he is better dispensed with and put out of the way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only keep an authorial narrator or a prescribed point of view if that stance adds to the effect or is required by the subject. When a narrator is unnecessary he may be omitted to give the reader a direct view; conversely, where the narrator 'makes the most of' the subject (economy, pictorial summary) he is a positive value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match method to the scope/amount of the subject
rubrics_metrics.description: It is simply a question of amount, of quantity, of the reach of the subject. If it passes a certain point it exceeds the capacity of the straight and dramatic method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large, panoramic, extensive subjects (chronicles, crowd-filled narratives, wide time/space reach) generally require a narrator and summary perspective; compact, limited subjects that center on an action or situation can often be treated dramatically, scene by scene. Choose the method according to the subject’s reach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodical consistency (single method where appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Awkward Age... chose to treat this story as pure drama; he never once draws upon the characteristic resource of the novelist... The whole of the book passes scenically before the reader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When feasible, commit to a single method (e.g., pure drama) to achieve cleanness and direct force. Consistency can give a story a 'hard, pure edge.' But recognize difficulty: strict adherence to one method is demanding and often novelists mix methods for practical reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary authorial intrusion or spokesman
rubrics_metrics.description: The spokesman has his way too often... sometimes he actually embarrasses it, when a matter of vivid drama is violently forced into the form of a narration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not let an omniscient commentator or authorial voice intrude where the scene could show the matter. Intrusive commentary can dilute or embarrass dramatic immediacy; prefer letting events speak unless commentary is required for effect or clarification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Let scenes embody appeals and implications rather than state them
rubrics_metrics.description: The scene has embodied it; the cheerless little room and the falling light and Densher’s uneasy movements and Susan's flushed, rain-splashed earnestness have all contributed; the broken phrases...have revealed its contour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Construct scenes so that appeals, motives, and moral dilemmas emerge from the accumulated particulars (setting, staging, tone) instead of being spelled out. The reader should 'live with' the appeal through the scene's enactment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognize the limits of the dramatic method
rubrics_metrics.description: Drama cannot always do everything in a novel, even where the heart of the story seems to lie in its action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether pure scenic presentation can supply necessary background, complexity, or retrospection; some subjects require narration, recapitulation, or reflective distance that drama alone cannot provide. Be candid about drama's limitations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use narrator when subject benefits from pictorial summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A large, loose, manifold subject, extensive in time and space, full of crowds and diversions, is a pictorial subject and can be nothing else... the angle of vision being assigned to the narrator.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply narrator/omniscient viewpoint to give general surveys, summaries, and panoramic impressions that dramatization cannot feasibly show. The narrator can supply economy and necessary perspective for broad subjects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct view unless a seer/recorder adds distinct value
rubrics_metrics.description: Where other things are equal a direct view of the matter in hand is the best.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When no distinctive value accrues from mediation, present events directly (dramatically) to the reader rather than through a mediator. Only retain mediation if it contributes a clear, justifiable effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare and deliberately approach turns of events (undercutting flat impressions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The undercutting...is seen wherever a turn of events is carefully prepared and deliberately approached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build and stage the moments that reveal deeper truths so the reader can perceive the depth by inference and accumulation, rather than by sudden explanation. Careful preparation gives substance and 'third dimension' to characters and situations; avoid abrupt, unearned revelations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make necessary background and singular settings sufficiently visible
rubrics_metrics.description: Nanda’s little world would be descried behind the scene without any further picturing... Nanda’s world is not the kind of society that can be taken for granted; for the purposes of her story it is important that her setting should be clearly seen and known.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a story’s particular background or social milieu is essential to understanding the subject, ensure it is made effective—either by dramatizing it in scenes or by measured narration. Do not assume every setting will be 'descried' implicitly; supply what the reader needs.
